subject: Request: early release + staged offboarding protections
messages:
From: Danielle Rogers <danielle@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Chen <mike.chen@acmehealth.com>, contracts@acmehealth.com
Date: Sat, 31 Oct 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: early release + staged offboarding protections

Hannah —

Thanks for being flexible on the timeline. We ran into an unexpected budget recon this quarter and leadership is asking if we can reduce committed capacity earlier than planned. We want to avoid a hard termination but need a path to step down our committed throughput over the next 60–90 days.

High-level ask:
- Reduce committed GPU pool by ~40% starting Dec 1, 2026, finalizing on Feb 1, 2027 (staged reduction).
- Lock remaining pre-paid credits in escrow so they can be used for migration support/credits during offboard.
- Keep dedicated SLA until final offboard date.

We understand this is non-standard. Can you share what concessions/redlines would be acceptable from Redwood to enable this staged offboard (and any fees or credit adjustments)? We prefer a written amendment rather than full contract termination.

Attachments: none on our side right now.

Appreciate quick guidance so we can present to our CFO on Monday.

—Danielle
Procurement Manager, Acme Health
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Danielle Rogers <danielle@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: early release + staged offboarding protections

Marissa / Karthik — forwarding Acme's ask. TL;DR: they want a 40% committed reduction (Dec 1 start), escrow of remaining credits, and SLA retained until final date. They want an amendment not a termination.

Quick thoughts:
- Commercially we can offer a staged reduction but need to protect unit economics — suggest a monthly staged reduction (e.g., 20% -> 20% -> remaining) not an immediate 40% drop.
- Escrow/locked credits is doable if we formalize permitted use (migration support, professional services credits) and cap refunds.
- Need executive sign-off for any one-time credit/waiver and for changing the ramp (non-standard).

Proposed immediate ask for approval:
1) Allow a 3-month staged ramp: 30% reduction 12/01, additional 10% 01/01, finalize 02/01.
2) Hold remaining pre-paid credits in escrow for 180 days and permit use for migration or professional services only.
3) One-time concession: 10% account credit (applied against final invoice) to ease transition.

I flagged a few items in the attached escalation summary (escalation_summary.xlsx). Please confirm whether we should propose this as a SOW amendment + early_release_agreement, and if we need exec approval for the credit + escrow.

—Hannah
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Danielle Rogers <danielle@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 13:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: early release + staged offboarding protections

Thanks Hannah — I reviewed their ask and the numbers. A few points and an alternative that protects revenue while being customer-friendly: 

1) Staggered cadence: we can do a 60-day notice to change committed levels with a maximum 25% reduction per 30-day window (so: 25% on 12/01, remaining 15% on 01/01). This preserves predictability.
2) Escrow: agree to hold pre-paid credits in an escrow pool but only allow redemptions for Redwood PS work or extended support during migration; unused escrow after 180 days converts to account credit that cannot be refunded.
3) One-time liquidity credit: offer a single 7.5% account credit vs. Hannah's 10% proposal.
4) Require an early_release_agreement signed by an exec (we should route to VP Sales for sign-off).

This deviates from standard T&Cs (escrow & staged reductions). We need explicit executive approval for the credit + escrow language and for bending the ramp-change notice period. Attached is a redline (redline_ramp_schedule.docx) showing the proposed ramp schedule and draft SOW amendment language — please review.

If we get exec approval we should: 1) update HubSpot with amendment, 2) generate SOW amendment + DocuSign, 3) schedule a 15-min call with Acme to confirm.

—Karthik
Sr. Director, Deal Desk
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Danielle Rogers <danielle@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: Approval request for staged offboarding + escrowed credits (Acme Health, ACME-2026-Q4-1427)

Vivek — escalating for exec approval. Summary below and recommended approval language.

Summary: Acme Health (large existing Dedicated customer) requests to reduce committed capacity earlier than contracted start of ramp-down. They want escrow of remaining pre-paid credits and retention of SLA through final offboard. Their proposed dates push final change to 02/01/2027.

Commercial impact: ~40% reduction in committed spend over 3 months if approved; short-term revenue delta offset by one-time credit (7.5%) and elongated SLA period.

Recommended approval (asks for your sign-off):
- Approve a SOW amendment that:
  * Permits a staged reduction capped at 25% per 30-day window (as per Karthik's redline).
  * Holds pre-paid credits in escrow for 180 days, redeemable only for Redwood PS or migration support.
  * Issues a single 7.5% account credit applied to the next invoice as migration support.
  * Requires customer to sign the early_release_agreement_v1.pdf and SOW amendment via DocuSign (link below) before changes take effect.
- Operational asks: Neha to log amendment in HubSpot and mark the seat/throughput changes. Karthik to send DocuSign and redline doc to customer.

Links: DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/embedded/abcdef123456
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/ACME-1427
Attachments: redline_ramp_schedule.docx, escalation_summary.xlsx, early_release_agreement_v1.pdf

Can you confirm approval or provide alternate guardrails? Need a yes/no by 10:00am PT so we can respond to Acme before their CFO sync.

—Marissa
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Danielle Rogers <danielle@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Approval request for staged offboarding + escrowed credits (Acme Health, ACME-2026-Q4-1427)

Thanks team — I reviewed the summary and proposed guardrails. Conditional approval granted with the following requirements: 

1) Approve the SOW amendment with the 25% per 30-day cap, escrow language (180 days, redeemable only for PS/migration), and the one-time 7.5% credit as proposed.
2) The concession is timeboxed: special pricing and credit is valid only if the customer signs the early_release_agreement_v1.pdf and SOW amendment within 7 calendar days of DocuSign transmission.
3) Add a rollback clause: if customer re-commits to previous committed levels within 6 months, the one-time credit will be reclaimed (applied as negative invoice).
4) Neha to add a Deal Desk note and update deal status in HubSpot (deal id ACME-2026-Q4-1427) and attach the signed amendment. Karthik to own DocuSign send and tracker.

Once signed, we should schedule a 15-minute transition call (Hannah to coordinate) and ensure Ops has the seat reduction schedule.

Approved by: Vivek Kulkarni, VP Sales (on behalf of Exec Committee)

—Vivek
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
